summary.goal: Extend the schema with plan-level 'understanding' (agent observations), plan-level 'context' (formalized decisions), and step-level 'specification' (architecture/design/testing/security details) to support the Intake -> Planner -> Orchestrator pipeline
summary.context: Current schema only has summary + steps. We need richer structure to capture ideation insights, formalized decisions, and formal specs. The information flow is: understanding (observations) -> context (decisions) -> specification (implementation).

model.understanding: Plan-level - what agents observed during ideation (observations, keywords, questions, concerns per role)
model.context: Plan-level - formalized decisions per role that inform step-level specs (designer: library/theme/patterns, architect: tech_stack/api_style/boundaries, tester: framework/strategy, security: auth/compliance)
model.specification: Step-level - each step can have its own architecture decisions, design elements, test cases, security requirements

information_flow.description: Three-stage refinement from loose to precise

stages.content: Loose observations, questions, concerns from agent ideation
Formalized choices that emerged from understanding

in_scope: Zod schemas for Understanding (plan-level) - agent observations
Zod schemas for Context (plan-level) - role-keyed decisions
Zod schemas for Specification (step-level) - implementation details
Database migration adding JSONB columns for all three
API endpoints for reading/updating understanding, context, and step specifications
Understanding tab in PlanEditorPage showing agent observations
Context tab in PlanEditorPage showing formalized decisions per role
Tabbed specification editor in StepEditor (Details | Architecture | Design | Testing | Security)
out_of_scope: Automatic agent population of understanding (manual for now)
Automatic derivation of context from understanding

acceptance_criteria.description: PlanVersion schema includes optional 'understanding' field (record of role -> AgentObservations)
PlanVersion schema includes optional 'context' field (record of role -> RoleContext)
Step schema includes optional 'specification' field with architecture, design, testing, security sub-schemas
Database stores understanding and context at plan_versions level, specification in steps JSONB
GET /plans/:id/versions/:version returns understanding, context, and steps with specification
PlanEditorPage has Understanding tab and Context tab (Plan | Understanding | Context)
StepEditor shows tabbed spec editor when expanded (Details | Architecture | Design | Testing | Security)
Understanding tab displays observations, keywords, questions, concerns per role
Context tab displays formalized decisions per role with structured fields
Step spec tabs allow inline editing of each domain's structured fields
Existing plans without understanding/context/specification continue to work (backward compatible)
MCP tools can read and write understanding, context, and step specifications

cases.description: Create plan -> PATCH understanding for 'architect' role -> GET returns understanding.architect
Create plan -> PATCH context for 'designer' role -> GET returns context.designer
Create plan with steps -> PATCH specification/architecture on step -> GET returns step.specification.architecture
PATCH understanding merges arrays (new observations appended, not replaced)
PATCH context merges fields (new fields added, existing preserved)
Existing plans without understanding/context load correctly with empty objects
PATCH understanding/context on approved plan returns 400
Understanding tab shows AgentObservationCard per role with correct confidence badge color
Context tab shows RoleContextCard per role with structured fields
Expanded step shows 5 tabs; Architecture tab displays decisions list
Empty understanding/context shows appropriate empty state messages

data_requirements: Plan with existing understanding (architect role with observations)
Plan with existing context (designer role with library decision)

tester.strategy: Integration tests at API and UI boundaries. Unit tests covered in individual feature implementation steps.
